cards.name: Pixel Aspect Ratio Correction
cards.summary: Toggles on-screen correction for a document whose pixel aspect ratio is not Square: when on, Photoshop stretches or squeezes the display so non-square video pixels look as they will on a TV or video monitor, without changing the stored pixels. The harvest found it disabled in every scratch state (all square-pixel documents), so it needs a document set to a non-square ratio under View > Pixel Aspect Ratio first.
use_for: painting on an HDV 1080 or anamorphic video frame without it looking squeezed
switching the stretch off to inspect the real stored pixels of a video still before export
comparing an SD lower-third graphic with and without the aspect correction
avoid: square-pixel documents for web, print or full-raster HD: the command stays disabled and is not needed
converting a non-square frame to square pixels for good: resample with Image > Image Size, then set View > Pixel Aspect Ratio > Square
cards.script_api: No confirmed route. The label-matched candidate app.runMenuItem(stringIDToTypeID('toggleProofVideo')) failed live with 'General Photoshop error occurred. This functionality may not be available in this version of Photoshop', followed by a note that the command "Select" is not currently available; the item was disabled in every state the harvest tried, so it may work on a non-square document (unverified). UXP (unverified): require('photoshop').core.performMenuCommand({commandID: 1112}). To make the item available from a script, first set app.activeDocument.pixelAspectRatio (writable in the PS API harvest) to a non-square value (unverified).

review.changes: script_api: quoted the harvested error (a general error that names the Select command, not this one); added the unverified UXP performMenuCommand route from extra.uxp_command_id and the PS API harvest's writable Document.pixelAspectRatio as the way to get the item enabled; use_for / avoid: dropped unharvested frame sizes (1440x1080, 1920x1080)

cards.name: Anamorphic 2:1 (2)
cards.summary: Assigns the 2 pixel aspect ratio of 2x anamorphic film footage to the document: each stored pixel is treated as twice as wide as it is tall. With Pixel Aspect Ratio Correction on, the canvas is displayed stretched to double width so it previews as it will on a video display. The pixel dimensions are not resampled; only how the pixels are interpreted and shown changes. Needs an open document.
use_for: a title card or matte painting to drop into 2x anamorphic film footage
retouching a still frame exported from an anamorphic sequence without it looking squeezed
previewing how squeezed anamorphic plates will look once unsqueezed in the edit
avoid: web, social or print graphics: keep Square pixels, since non-square documents look distorted in browsers and image viewers
video with a different squeeze (HDV 1.33, DVCPRO HD 1.5): pick the matching preset or the frame is stretched wrongly

use_for: checking yellows, oranges and greens in a print design carry the expected yellow
spotting stray yellow in a cool blue sky or in neutral greys
checking fine yellow text, which is hard to judge in the composite
avoid: the full press result: use Working CMYK

cards.name: Rulers
cards.summary: Shows or hides the rulers along the top and left edges of the document window; units follow Preferences > Units & Rulers (right-click a ruler to change them), and dragging out of a ruler creates a guide. Needs an open document.
use_for: measuring margins and bleed on a print flyer or business card
dragging guides to set up a poster or social-post layout grid
placing a logo a set distance from the edges of a banner
avoid: exact numeric placement: use the Properties panel or New Guide Layout instead of eyeballing on the rulers

cards.name: Full Screen Mode
cards.summary: Switches the document window to full screen with no menu bar, title bar, scroll bars or panels, on a black background, for viewing the image distraction-free; panels can still be revealed at the screen edges. Needs an open document.
use_for: presenting a poster or key visual to a client on screen without the interface
judging a photo retouch or composition at the largest possible size
a clean full-screen screenshot or screen-recording of a design
